principals.description: Provider-independent application principal for one human identity at one issuer; its UUID is the stable identity referenced by memberships, ownership and audit.
principals.lifecycle: Created at first verified login; never deleted by the runtime. Disablement is a state change. Retention and erasure follow PH-13.

id.description: Application-generated immutable principal UUID, written to the provider's administrator-only attribute and asserted by access tokens as orion_principal_id.

issuer.description: Exact OIDC issuer that authenticated this principal; together with subject it is the provider association.

subject.description: Provider-assigned stable subject identifier at the issuer; never used as the application identity.

status.description: ACTIVE principals can hold sessions; DISABLED principals are globally denied within the 30-second revocation bound.

display_name.description: Presentation name from the last verified login; never used as identity or authorization evidence.
display_name.nullMeaning: No bounded display name has been obtained from a verified login.

verified_email.description: Presentation email snapshot from the last verified login; never used to link accounts, grant access or accept invitations.
verified_email.nullMeaning: No bounded verified email snapshot has been obtained.

objects.principals_issuer_subject_key: One application principal per provider identity; concurrent first logins converge on one row.
objects.principals_issuer_nonblank: Issuer is an absolute HTTP(S) URL without whitespace.
objects.principals_disabled_state: A disablement instant exists exactly for disabled principals.
objects.principals_display_name_nonblank: A presentation name, when present, cannot be blank.
objects.principals_verified_email_nonblank: A verified-login email snapshot, when present, cannot be blank.

human_sessions.description: Server-managed browser session: an opaque cookie credential's hash, its bounds and assurance, and the sealed provider tokens obtained for it.
human_sessions.lifecycle: Created at login as ACTIVE, or PENDING_LIMIT when the principal already has five active sessions; REVOKED rows are retained without deletion until a retention rule is approved under PH-13.

id.description: Backend-generated session UUID, shown to its owner for session management and bound into sealed tokens and CSRF tokens.

token_hash.description: SHA-256 of the 32-byte random cookie credential; the recoverable credential is never stored.

state.description: PENDING_LIMIT may only list and end sessions; ACTIVE may call protected operations; REVOKED is terminal.

provider_session_id.description: Provider session identifier (OIDC sid) used to apply back-channel logout.
provider_session_id.nullMeaning: The provider did not report a session identifier.

assurance_level.description: Authentication context class (acr) asserted by the ID token verified at login.

authenticated_at.description: Provider-reported instant of the user's authentication (auth_time) for this session.

strong_authenticated_at.description: Instant of the latest strong authentication verified for this session, used for recent-authentication checks.
strong_authenticated_at.nullMeaning: No strong authentication has been verified for this session.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: Inactivity bound applied to this session: 1800 for administrative contexts or principals without memberships, 7200 for operator-only access.

created_at.description: PostgreSQL-clock instant the session was created.

last_activity_at.description: PostgreSQL-clock instant of the latest recorded human activity; background requests do not advance it, and writes are throttled to 15 seconds.

absolute_expires_at.description: Instant after which the session is invalid regardless of activity, at most 12 hours after creation.

provider_tokens.description: Provider access, refresh and ID tokens sealed with AES-256-GCM under the session key ring and bound to the session ID.

access_token_expires_at.description: Database-clock estimate of the sealed access token's expiry, five seconds earlier than the provider's lifetime.

provider_checked_at.description: Latest instant the provider confirmed the session through introspection, refresh or login.

refresh_lease_until.description: End of the single-flight lease held by the request refreshing provider tokens.

revoked_at.description: PostgreSQL-clock instant the session was revoked.
revoked_at.nullMeaning: The session has not been revoked.

revocation_reason.description: Why the session ended: logout, user termination, expiry, replacement, provider logout or inactivity, refresh rejection, principal disablement or principal mismatch.
revocation_reason.nullMeaning: The session has not been revoked.

objects.human_sessions_principal_id_fkey: A session belongs to an existing principal; principals cannot be deleted while sessions exist.
objects.human_sessions_token_hash_key: One session per cookie credential; supports lookup by credential hash.
objects.human_sessions_principal_state_idx: Supports counting and listing a principal's sessions by state.
objects.human_sessions_provider_session_idx: Supports back-channel logout by provider session identifier.
objects.human_sessions_token_hash_sha256: Credential hash is exactly one SHA-256 digest.
objects.human_sessions_idle_bounds: Inactivity bound stays between one minute and the two-hour operator maximum.
objects.human_sessions_absolute_after_creation: Absolute expiry follows creation by at most the selected 12-hour maximum.
objects.human_sessions_revocation_state: Revocation instant and reason exist exactly for revoked sessions.
objects.human_sessions_revocation_reason_known: Revocation reason is one of the documented values.

oidc_login_attempts.description: Single-use binding between a browser login-attempt cookie and the OIDC state, nonce and PKCE verifier of one authorization request.
oidc_login_attempts.lifecycle: Created when a login starts, consumed once by the callback and expired after 10 minutes; expired rows are retained until a cleanup rule is approved.

id.description: Backend-generated attempt UUID that binds the sealed secrets.

handle_hash.description: SHA-256 of the random login-attempt cookie value.

state.description: OIDC state value expected back at the callback.

secrets.description: PKCE code verifier and OIDC nonce sealed with AES-256-GCM and bound to the attempt ID.

return_to.description: Validated same-origin relative path to open after a successful login.

requested_assurance.description: Authentication context class (acr) this login requested, such as the strong teluni-aal2 level for step-up.
requested_assurance.nullMeaning: A standard login without a requested level.

max_age_seconds.description: Maximum authentication age requested from the provider; 0 forces a new authentication for recent-authentication checks.

expires_at.description: Instant after which the callback can no longer consume the attempt.

consumed_at.description: Instant the callback consumed the attempt; a second use is rejected.
consumed_at.nullMeaning: The attempt has not been used.

objects.oidc_login_attempts_handle_hash_key: One attempt per browser handle; supports consumption by handle.
objects.oidc_login_attempts_handle_sha256: Handle hash is exactly one SHA-256 digest.
objects.oidc_login_attempts_state_nonblank: State uses the base64url alphabet and cannot be blank.
objects.oidc_login_attempts_return_relative: Return path is relative to the panel origin.
objects.oidc_login_attempts_expiry_bounds: An attempt expires after creation and within 10 minutes.
objects.oidc_login_attempts_max_age_bounds: Requested maximum authentication age cannot be negative.

backchannel_logout_replays.description: Identifiers of accepted provider logout tokens, kept to reject a replayed token.
backchannel_logout_replays.lifecycle: Inserted when a logout token is accepted; rows past expires_at may be deleted because the token is then too old to be accepted.

jti.description: Unique identifier (jti) of an accepted logout token.

received_at.description: PostgreSQL-clock instant the token was accepted.

expires_at.description: Instant after which the token would fail the five-minute age check, so its record is no longer needed.

objects.backchannel_logout_replays_pkey: Each logout token is accepted at most once.
objects.backchannel_logout_replays_expiry_after_: A replay record expires after it was received.

enums.PrincipalStatus: Global principal state: ACTIVE or DISABLED.
enums.HumanSessionState: Server-managed session state: PENDING_LIMIT, ACTIVE or REVOKED.
